thesis: The workshop makes exactness, soundness, relational dependence and research accountability explicit through proofs and counterexamples.
role: Appendices reinforce the central argument and prescribe auditable reporting.

ideas.statement: Exact continuation depends on closed summary updates, observable results and preserved admissibility; the proof does not establish small or learnable summaries.
Sound abstraction supports rejecting impossible branches, while accepting a candidate requires a concrete witness or stronger representation.
Independent projections may invent combinations; a relational vocabulary can preserve the lost dependency compactly.
Exercises distinguish semantic types, question-relative sufficiency, provenance, empirical samples, budget failure and causal intervention.
Publishable results must disclose domain, supplied and learned components, proof level, complete cost, failures and possible refutations.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: A sum needs a count to determine a mean; neither determines whether all elements were equal.
Two articles copying one report are not independent confirmations.
Accumulating exceptions may be memory rather than structural learning.
Faster prepared queries must be evaluated together with compilation and update costs.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: A selection policy using hidden state is not covered automatically by the summary induction.
A certificate does not certify the external truth of premises.

audit.notes: Read every unit; preserve proposed versus demonstrated status.
